_meta.purpose: Freeze the candidate portfolio recipe BEFORE any holdout data (2025-04-01 onward) is touched. This file is the one-shot contract for H2.
_meta.note_dev_window_offset: 2021-11-07 was the --start CLI flag; both artifacts' first RETURN row is 2021-11-08. carry_audit artifacts use window start 2021-11-08 (first return day, since day-0 has no prior close); factor_floor/directional artifacts use 2021-11-07 as the --start flag but likewise produce their first return row at 2021-11-08 (the factor_floor daily_returns.csv's first row is a 0.0/0.0 warm-up bar). Both are the same dev window; the 1-day offset between the CLI --start flag and the first return row is inherent to each pipeline's return-construction (a t-1 price is needed to form day-1 return) and is not a discrepancy to reconcile.

carry.construction: always-on funding-carry sleeve: short 1x perp + long 1x spot, equal notional both legs, 50/50 BTC/ETH; inception = first day of window, exit = last day; margin = 1/3 of perp notional (realized leverage <= 3x by construction)

stressed_cost_model.turnover_convention: 'per side' = one execution (open OR close) touching both legs: spot(taker+spread) + perp(taker+spread) = 0.0016; inception charges one open, final exit one close.
stressed_cost_model.rebalance_trigger: rebalance fires when |drift| >= drift_threshold_frac_of_target (0.2, i.e. 20% of target per-leg notional)
stressed_cost_model.rebalance_drift_convention: drift tracked by compounding each leg's equity with its own daily return since the last rebalance: long-spot leg grows at +spot_ret, SHORT-perp leg grows at -perp_ret (a short's equity FALLS as the perp price rises). This is the drift-generating reading (the alternative, +perp_ret, makes the short leg track spot so drift never reaches 20% and rebalance count degenerates to 0). AMBIGUITY WAS RESOLVED THIS WAY in the §C2 costs pass; carried forward unchanged into the holdout.
stressed_cost_model.rebalance_cost: full round-trip cost (2x open = 0.0032) charged on the drift notional at each rebalance event
stressed_cost_model.margin_cost: constant daily risk-free drag = rf_daily * (1/3) * perp_notional (margin_fraction_of_perp_notional = 1/3, i.e. leverage <= 3x)
stressed_cost_model.boundary_basis: recorded as 0.0 by construction — compute_price_pnl marks the spot-perp basis to market every day via spot_ret - perp_ret on actual price series, so entry/exit basis convergence is already inside the hedge P&L. A separate boundary-basis charge would double-count.

carry.dev_window_stressed_sr_note: = plus_margin_cost = plus_boundary_basis layer (final stressed value), read from costs.json 'stressed_blended_sr'. Reference only — NOT re-measured in this file; recomputed fresh on the holdout window in H2.
carry.gate_caveat_carried_forward: the rebalance-convention choice above plausibly overstates rebalance cost ~3x (§39 caveat: stressed SR is realistically a range [3.75, ~5.9], with 3.75 the conservative/gate-relevant bound). The 3.75 bound and its convention are frozen for holdout evaluation — no re-tuning.

factor.status: SURVIVES ml_survival gate as the directional sleeve (LGB candidate did not beat it, see phase4_note)

signal.definition: ma_cross_signal(close, fast=10, slow=50) = sign(SMA_10 - SMA_50), both MAs ending at index t-1 (strictly causal: no same-bar look-ahead). Long-short: signal in {-1, 0, +1} per coin.
signal.universe: bitcoin + ethereum, equal weight (mean of the two coins' daily net-of-cost returns)

sizing_stack.note: V2 sizing primitives (tradingagents.strategies.v2_sizing), canonical constants exactly as scripts/factor_baselines.py module-level constants. NO trend filter is applied (the factor_baselines.py docstring is explicit: 'these ARE the trend strategies').
sizing_stack.kelly_note: 0.5, NOT 0.25. The F6 kelly=0.25 adoption (data/rebuild/axis_sizing/result.json) applied to the retired LGB candidate config only. The factor floor (macross_10_50_ls) was measured at kelly=0.5 in scripts/factor_baselines.py and that is the frozen, as-measured config for H2 — it is not re-tuned to kelly=0.25.
sizing_stack.halt_latch: run_coin_backtest's max_portfolio_dd = 0.15 circuit breaker: PERMANENT per-coin latch. Once a coin's drawdown-from-peak breaches 15%, halted=True never resets and every subsequent bar for that coin returns a flat 0.0. This is the live system's real circuit breaker; it is frozen ON, applied identically per coin, unchanged for holdout.
sizing_stack.halt_transparency_note: in the dev window both coins eventually halt (trailing zero tail = 759/1240 bars = 61%); full-series SR (the gate metric, 'sr' key) already reflects this. sr_active (+1.016, halt-tail excluded) is diagnostic only, never used for selection or gating.

factor.dev_window_sr_note: read from data/rebuild/factor_floor/BEST/daily_returns.csv 'portfolio' column and confirmed against directional_verdict.json floor.portfolio_full_series.sharpe (0.632). Reference only — recomputed fresh on the holdout window in H2.

allocation.rule: inverse-vol weights computed on DEV data only (2021-11-07/08 .. 2025-03-31), carry capped at 50% of book; factor gets the remainder. Rebalanced monthly during holdout on trailing-90d vol (see rebalance_rule below); cap always re-applied. Weights are recomputed at each calendar-month start from trailing-90-calendar-day sleeve vols (carry cap 0.5 reapplied), then HELD CONSTANT and applied to daily sleeve returns until the next rebalance date (no intra-month drift accounting).
allocation.formula: w_carry_raw = (1/vol_carry) / (1/vol_carry + 1/vol_factor); w_factor_raw = 1 - w_carry_raw; if w_carry_raw > 0.5: w_carry = 0.5, w_factor = 0.5; else w_carry = w_carry_raw, w_factor = w_factor_raw
allocation.vol_definition: annualized daily-return stdev, ddof=1, x sqrt(252)
allocation.zero_vol_guard: If a sleeve's trailing-90d vol is exactly 0 (halted/dead sleeve), its weight is 0; the surviving sleeve receives its capped weight (carry never exceeds 0.5); any remainder is cash (weight to no sleeve, zero return). If both are zero-vol, the portfolio is 100% cash from that rebalance date. This guard takes precedence over the inverse-vol formula above whenever it applies (the formula is undefined at vol=0) and is re-applied identically at the initial 50/50 freeze and at every monthly rebalance.

dev_window_computation.factor_input: data/rebuild/factor_floor/BEST/daily_returns.csv column 'portfolio' (1240 rows, 2021-11-08..2025-03-31, first row is a 0.0/0.0 warm-up bar)
dev_window_computation.sr_sanity_check: mean/std*sqrt(252) on these same series reproduces costs.json stressed_blended_sr (3.7503661753109525) and floor_table.md portfolio sr (0.6322181732492269) to ~1e-9 -- confirms the vol inputs are read from the correct, already-cost-adjusted / already-net series.

frozen_dev_weights.note: Carry's raw inverse-vol weight (94.1%) blows through the 50% cap because the stressed carry sleeve has ~16x lower realized vol than the factor sleeve in dev (0.69% vs 11.0% annualized) despite its much higher dev SR. The cap is therefore binding at the very first allocation point -- this is exactly the audit-unfriendly 'all eggs in the newest/quietest basket' scenario the cap in the task brief is designed to prevent. Both sleeves start at 50/50 in holdout.

rebalance_rule.frequency: monthly (recompute at each calendar month start during the holdout window)
rebalance_rule.vol_window: trailing 90 calendar days of realized daily returns per sleeve, as of the rebalance date
rebalance_rule.formula: identical to formula above, re-applied with trailing-90d vols in place of the full-dev-window vols
rebalance_rule.cap: carry weight capped at 50% of book at every rebalance, unconditionally -- same cap value as the dev freeze, never re-tuned
rebalance_rule.look_ahead_guard: trailing-90d window must end strictly before the rebalance date (no same-day or future data)
rebalance_rule.zero_vol_handling: see allocation.zero_vol_guard above -- applies identically at every monthly rebalance, not just the initial dev-window freeze

holdout_protocol.latch_convention: The 15% halt latch is an evaluation-window state, not inherited history. Every evaluation window starts with a fresh latch (halted=False, fresh peak equity). This matches the dev-window convention (F1 ran with fresh latch at 2021-11-07) and the carry sleeve's fresh holdout inception (2025-04-01). Rationale: the holdout simulates a Phase-4 deployment start, which begins with a fresh circuit breaker.
holdout_protocol.zero_variance_sr_convention: Any return series with zero variance over the evaluation window has SR defined as 0.0 for all gate and placebo comparisons (0/0 := 0, never NaN).
holdout_protocol.ledger_guard_edit_authorization: In addition to the three carry-script edits, H2 is authorized to add allow_holdout=True to log_trial calls (or a --allow-holdout CLI flag passing it through) in scripts/factor_baselines.py and scripts/carry_audit_costs.py. This is a mechanical guard-passage edit, touches no economic parameter, and is the ONLY place allow_holdout is ever used.
holdout_protocol.one_shot_rule: No parameter changes to either sleeve, the sizing stack, or the allocation rule after this file is committed -- regardless of the holdout outcome. Any ledger calls made against this evaluation MUST pass allow_holdout=True, and this is the ONLY evaluation ever permitted to set that flag.

steps.action: Extend OHLCV data through 2026-07-01 and run scripts/factor_baselines.py's macross_10_50_ls path (same builder, same sizing constants) in two stages per holdout_protocol.latch_convention: (a) compute the ma_cross_10_50 signal over the FULL history (2021-11-07..2026-07-01) so it is properly warmed up, then (b) run the halt-latch/sizing/backtest engine fresh, starting at 2025-04-01, over the holdout-window slice of that signal only.
steps.command: Stage 1 (signal warm-up, full history, engine output discarded): uv run python scripts/factor_baselines.py --start 2021-11-07 --end 2026-07-01 --output-dir data/rebuild/holdout/factor_floor_signal_only -- used ONLY to obtain a correctly warmed-up ma_cross_10_50 signal array through 2026-07-01. Stage 2 (fresh-latch engine, holdout window only): feed the 2025-04-01..2026-07-01 slice of that signal array into a FRESH invocation of the identical sizing/backtest path (build_positions_with_hold + run_coin_backtest, same constants), initialized at 2025-04-01 with halted=False, peak_equity=1.0, flat position -- this run's daily-return series is the frozen portfolio's factor-sleeve holdout output.
steps.warm_up_note: The MA-10/50 cross signal needs >=50 bars of prior Close history to be defined, so the signal itself is computed over the full 2021-11-07..2026-07-01 history (stage 1). Per holdout_protocol.latch_convention, the halt-latch/sizing/backtest engine is NOT carried in from dev -- it starts fresh at 2025-04-01 (halted=False for both coins, fresh peak equity), regardless of the dev-window halt dates recorded above (halt_dates_dev_window). This reverses the prior (rejected) convention, which carried the dev-window latch state into holdout and left both coins permanently halted for the entire holdout window -- a zero-variance degenerate result (see zero_variance_sr_convention and allocation.zero_vol_guard). Evaluating on a signal computed from a truncated (holdout-only) OHLCV input would instead leave the first ~50 holdout bars with an undefined (zero) signal -- also not a legitimate alternative -- hence the two-stage split.

steps.action: Run the C2 stressed construction (scripts/carry_audit_costs.py) over the holdout window ONLY -- START/END set directly to the holdout bounds (2025-04-01 / 2026-07-01), not extended forward from the dev-window run -- with identical cost parameters (see sleeves.carry.stressed_cost_model above, verbatim). Per holdout_protocol.latch_convention this is already a fresh, holdout-only inception with no carried-in state to reset (the carry sleeve is always-on and structurally has no latch).
steps.command: edit scripts/carry_audit_costs.py (or preferably a pass-through copy) START -> "2025-04-01", END -> "2026-07-01", and the output directory -> "data/rebuild/holdout/carry_audit/" -- no other changes -- then: uv run python scripts/carry_audit_costs.py
steps.note: carry_audit_costs.py has no --start/--end CLI flags; window is hardcoded at module scope (START, END = ...). H2 is permitted to change EXACTLY three things in scripts/carry_audit_costs.py (or preferably pass-through copies): START -> "2025-04-01", END -> "2026-07-01", and the output directory -> "data/rebuild/holdout/carry_audit/". All cost parameters remain frozen. Dev artifacts in data/rebuild/carry_audit/ must remain untouched; H2 must verify `git diff --stat data/rebuild/carry_audit/` is empty after the run. NOTE also: carry signal has no warm-up requirement (always-on), but funding/spot fetches need the holdout date range only -- unlike the factor sleeve, no pre-window history or output slicing is needed since START/END already equal the holdout window. See holdout_protocol.ledger_guard_edit_authorization for the additional permitted allow_holdout edit (log_trial calls / --allow-holdout flag).

steps.action: Combine the two sleeves' holdout daily returns with the frozen allocation rule (allocation.rule / allocation.rebalance_rule above): start both sleeves at 50/50 on the holdout's first bar, recompute weights monthly from trailing-90d vol, re-apply the 50% carry cap every time.
steps.output: a single holdout portfolio daily-return series and its Sharpe, total return, max drawdown.

criteria.sleeve_contribution_note: sleeve_contribution_i = sleeve i's cumulative net return over the holdout window (standalone, before weighting) must be >= 0.
criteria.placebo_scope_note: Scope: factor sleeve only (carry is model-free/always-on -- not placebo-testable; unchanged).
criteria.placebo_definition: Procedure: N=500 placebo variants, k=1..500. Variant k: per coin, block-shuffle the REAL macross_10_50_ls holdout signal array (int8 {-1,0,+1}) using the stationary-bootstrap index algorithm pinned in placebo_shuffle_algorithm below (geometric block lengths, mean 21, wraparound, truncate to T), applied to the SIGNAL arrays -- resample blocks of the signal series (preserving persistence + marginal distribution), same length as original. One numpy default_rng(seed=k) per variant; coins processed in fixed order [bitcoin, ethereum], drawing sequentially from that same rng (bitcoin's block-index draws consumed first, then ethereum's, for each variant k). Run each variant through the IDENTICAL frozen sizing/engine path as the real factor sleeve (same constants, costs, price stop, and the SAME fresh-latch convention as the real arm per holdout_protocol.latch_convention -- halted=False / fresh peak equity at the holdout's first bar for every placebo variant), BTC+ETH EW portfolio, holdout window -- real arm and placebo arms are structurally symmetric identical fresh-latch holdout-only engine runs, differing only in the block-shuffled signal array.
criteria.placebo_shuffle_algorithm: Block resampling uses the same stationary-bootstrap index algorithm as tradingagents/rebuild/compare.py paired_bootstrap (geometric block lengths, mean 21, wraparound, truncate to T) applied to the SIGNAL arrays; one numpy default_rng(seed=k) per variant, coins processed in fixed order [bitcoin, ethereum] drawing from that rng sequentially.
criteria.placebo_pvalue_formula: p = (1 + #{placebo portfolio SR >= real factor portfolio SR}) / (N + 1). Gate: p < 0.05. Per zero_variance_sr_convention, any zero-variance placebo or real-arm return series has SR = 0.0 in this comparison (never NaN).

steps.action: Record the holdout verdict (GO/NO-GO to deploy) in a new verdict JSON. Ledger entries for this evaluation must set allow_holdout=True -- the only evaluation in the rebuild ever permitted to do so.
